rounds.proof_sketch: N = 16384 = 512 * 32, so N is exactly divisible by 32. Original: (16384 + 31) / 32 = 16415 / 32 = 512. Mutated: (16384 + 30) / 32 = 16414 / 32 = 512. Both integer divisions truncate the fractional part to yield 512. The grid dimensions are identical.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the x-dimension grid calculation from (N + 31) / 32 to (N + 30) / 32. This ceiling-division formula would produce different results only when N ≡ 1 (mod 32), where the original formula would round up but the mutated formula would not. However, with the fixed shape N = 16384, which is exactly divisible by 32 (16384 = 512 × 32), both expressions evaluate to exactly 512. Since the kernel launch configuration is identical in both cases, the kernel executes with the same number of blocks and produces bitwise-identical results regardless of input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: The mutation is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The grid dimension difference would only manifest when N ≡ 1 (mod 32), causing the mutant to skip the last column of output elements. Since N = 16384 ≡ 0 (mod 32), this condition cannot be triggered. Killing this mutant would require changing N to a value like 16385.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing grid/block dimension calculations involving ceiling-division patterns like (N + K - 1) / K, test coverage should include dimensions that are NOT exact multiples of the tile size. For robust kernel testing, use prime or near-prime dimensions (e.g., 16385, 16383) to exercise boundary handling code paths.
